Apple on Friday filed a blockbuster lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing the company of stealing trade secrets. The initial filing contains many fascinating details, but one figure in particular caught my eye: the number of former Apple employees now working at OpenAI.

Over 400 Apple Employees Now Work at OpenAI

According to Apple's filing, more than 400 former Apple employees currently work at OpenAI. Apple therefore states that it is "unsurprising" that OpenAI staff would have knowledge of Apple's confidential information:

"Given that more than 400 former Apple employees now work at OpenAI, it is unsurprising that certain OpenAI personnel would have knowledge of Apple's confidential and proprietary information, and would have confidentiality obligations with respect to that information. OpenAI has, however, exploited that knowledge to extract further information from Apple's current employees and trusted partners, and has designed its interview process to elicit additional Apple confidential information — while simultaneously taking steps to conceal its conduct. The personnel OpenAI now employs were, until recently, trusted by Apple—"

Although Apple has not disclosed specific details, according to a Bloomberg report, we know that employees from countless teams within Apple have defected to OpenAI. Most recently, OpenAI poached Paul Meade, who had been leading the Apple Vision Pro and Apple smart glasses projects.

In fact, a Bloomberg report on Saturday noted that the "majority" of talent OpenAI has recruited from Apple came from the engineering division led by incoming Apple CEO John Ternus. The report also mentioned that OpenAI's hardware chief and former Apple design chief Tang Tan had a "tense" relationship with Ternus during his time at Apple.

The outcome of Apple's case against OpenAI remains to be seen. Either way, this is shaping up to be a fascinating prolonged battle—especially once the case enters the discovery phase. What are your thoughts on the lawsuit? Let us know in the comments.
